cia.title: CURRICULUM, INSTRUCTION, AND ASSESSMENT MONITORING CHECKLIST

items.text: 1. MELC mapping (Planned vs Taught vs Assessed) is conducted
2. All MELCs are reflected in lesson plans
3. Assessments are aligned with taught MELCs
4. High-frequency NAT MELCs are prioritized
1. Classroom tests include 40–50% HOTS items
2. Test items reflect application, analysis, interpretation
3. NAT-like test items are used
4. Item analysis is conducted after assessments

2. Vocabulary is pre-taught before lessons
3. Learners explain answers in words
4. Learners justify solutions/answers

2. Learners are grouped based on skill gaps
3. Remediation activities are focused and MELC-based
4. Progress of learners is regularly monitored

3. Instruction is adjusted based on data
4. LAC minutes reflect data-based decisions

3. LRs include embedded assessment (rubrics/checks)
4. School conducts LR pre-validation
5. CID-validated LRs are used in lessons

4. Evidence of implementation is available for TA Round 2

2. Priority gaps are clearly identified

tqpd.title: TEACHER QUALITY AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT MONITORING CHECKLIST

items.text: 1. School conducted PD needs analysis using learner data
2. Priority LAC/INSET topics (2–3 only) are clearly identified
3. PD plan aligns with curriculum, assessment, and remediation gaps
4. School conducted PD needs analysis using learner data
1. LAC sessions are conducted regularly (monthly)
2. LAC sessions focus on 1–2 priority issues only
3. LACs use interactive strategies (lesson study, peer sharing, planning)
4. Teachers actively participate (not lecture-style sessions)
5. LAC outputs (lesson plans, strategies, materials) are produced
1. INSET program is based on LAC outputs and identified needs
2. INSET sessions deepen learning (not repetition of LAC topics)
3. Appropriate resource persons are utilized
4. INSET program is aligned with division and school priorities
1. 100% teacher participation in LAC sessions
2. 100% teacher participation in INSET
3. Sessions are scheduled within official time
4. Blended/alternative modalities are used when needed
1. Teachers prepare post-LAC/INSET action plans
2. Revised lesson plans reflect new strategies
3. Improved assessment practices are evident
4. Classroom practices reflect LAC/INSET learning (based on observation)
5. Teachers share results/experiences in succeeding LAC sessions
1. LAC attendance and minutes are complete and updated
2. INSET reports and documentation are available
3. Teacher action plans are compiled and monitored
4. Documentation is used to plan follow-up actions

sections.name: G. INSTRUCTIONAL LEADERSHIP (ROLE OF SCHOOL HEAD)

items.text: 1. School head ensures 100% participation
2. School head monitors LAC/INSET outputs and application
3. School head actively participates in PD sessions
4. Follow-through actions are implemented and tracked
1. Potential scholarship applicants are identified
2. Mentoring system is established (with assigned mentors)
3. Mentoring sessions are conducted and documented
4. Teachers maintain updated portfolios (lesson plans, assessments, data)
5. Re-entry plans are required for endorsed applicants

sections.name: I. LEARNING RESOURCE (LR) UTILIZATION AND SUPPORT

items.text: 1. School conducted LR utilization/needs assessment
2. LRs are aligned with MELCs and lesson objectives
3. Teachers use print, digital, and OER strategically
4. LRs are integrated in instruction, assessment, and remediation
5. LR use is discussed and reflected in LAC sessions

sections.name: J. IMPACT ON TEACHING AND LEARNING (HIGH-LEVEL CHECK)

items.text: 1. Teaching practices show improvement (based on observation)
2. Assessment quality has improved (HOTS, alignment)
3. Learner engagement is evident
4. Evidence of improved learner performance is available

ldp.title: LEARNER DEVELOPMENT AND PROTECTION MONITORING CHECKLIST

sections.name: A. IDENTIFY (Early Identification of At-Risk Learners)

items.text: 1. Attendance (SF2), academic (SF5), and behavior data are regularly reviewed
2. Teachers maintain classroom learner tracking sheets
3. School has a master list of at-risk learners
4. At-risk learners are profiled (academic, behavioral, socio-economic factors)
5. Root cause analysis is conducted for identified learners
6. School Learner Tracking Team (SLTT) is organized and functional
7. Targeted remediation programs are implemented (not general review)
8. Learners are grouped based on specific learning gaps
9. Differentiated instruction strategies are evident in teaching
10. Peer tutoring or learning buddy system is implemented
11. Counseling or psychosocial support is provided when needed
12. Intervention plans are documented per learner/group
13. Appropriate and contextualized learning materials are used

sections.name: C. ENGAGE (Safe, Inclusive, and Supportive Environment)

items.text: 14. SEL (Social-Emotional Learning) is integrated in daily lessons
15. Teachers use strategies that develop self- awareness and relationships
16. Classroom environment promotes respect and inclusivity
17. Positive discipline practices are observed (no punitive approach)
18. Child Protection Committee (CPC) is active and functional
19. Anti-bullying and child protection programs are implemented
20. Learners are given opportunities to express ideas and feelings
21. Monthly monitoring of learner attendance and performance is conducted
22. Learner tracking records are regularly updated
23. SLTT conducts quarterly review meetings
24. Interventions are adjusted based on learner progress
25. Formative assessments are used to track improvement
26. Reduction in number of at-risk learners is monitored
27. Parents are regularly informed of learner progress
28. Parent conferences for at-risk learners are conducted
29. Home visitation is implemented for frequent absentees
30. School coordinates with barangay/community stakeholders
31. LAC sessions discuss learner cases and interventions
32. Best practices are documented and shared
